p: Our father, Sri Umakant, passed away suddenly because of diabetes-related complications.
In his memory, we decided to help other families facing the same illness.
Sri Umakant was a philanthropist and a man of principle. A former member of the Indian Air Force, he taught us through his actions to serve humanity.

He was a charter member of the Rotary Club of Sitapur when the club was formed in the year 1969. He was the charter president of the Rotary Club during the formation of the Rotaract Club in Sitapur district. He was also the Uttar Pradesh secretary of the Sri Aurobindo Ashram, Pondicherry, and an active member of the Annie Besant Society and the Theosophical Society in India.

Through the Rotary Club, he was closely involved in polio vaccination drives in the 1970s and early 1980s. He personally collected the polio drops from Lucknow airport, about 100 kilometres from Sitapur, and brought them in his own vehicle so that children could be vaccinated. He also took part in cataract eradication initiatives, under which many eye camps were held in the rural villages of Sitapur district.

p: Diabetes and cardiovascular and metabolic diseases affect many families.
We also found that Uttar Pradesh lacks enough trained medical and paramedical professionals.

chapters.alt: Photograph of a rally of students in white uniforms walking along a street with placards
p: In 2021, we set up a social and charitable trust to help people suffering from diabetes and from cardiovascular and metabolic diseases.
We organize continuous medical education programmes and workshops for the medical and paramedical fraternity.
They learn about the latest technologies and available drugs.

chapters.alt: Photograph of a woman with a child receiving a kit of items at a table, with several men standing and seated nearby
p: We run free medical camps on a continuing basis for poor and needy people with diabetes and with cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, and we support the treatment of poor patients.
Our aim is to provide free or concessional treatment by setting up hospitals and medical institutions.

chapters.alt: Photograph of a group of people gathered around a sapling being planted
p: For a healthier environment, we have helped plant trees across Uttar Pradesh and the rest of India.
Because children are the future of the country, we support poor students' education by helping with fee payments, and we aim to create affordable educational institutions in the future.
We also work for animal welfare and for the socio-economic upliftment of rural communities.
Our resources are modest, but our commitment is not. We keep going, one camp and one programme at a time.
